findings.issue: The card-list construction rule (refId extraction, `id > 10000` alternate-form exclusion, dedupe, sort by id) is duplicated across the type, move and ability queries plus type membership
findings.suggestion: Extract one helper, e.g. `cardsFromRefs(entries: {pokemon?: NamedRef}[], extras?)` built on the species directory, so list construction and form-exclusion rules live in one place

findings.issue: The short_effect → flavor-text → '—' fallback chain is copy-pasted in getMovePageData and getAbilityPageData
findings.suggestion: Extract `englishEffect(effectEntries, flavorEntries)` into lib/format.ts next to latestEnglishFlavor

findings.issue: Rendering is a key-based if-chain that duplicates the column metadata declared in queries.ts (app/src/lib/queries.ts:636-645); adding/renaming a column requires synchronized edits in both files
findings.suggestion: Ship a render function or cell component with each column definition ({key, label, render}) so the server's columns array drives rendering end-to-end

findings.issue: Caching policy is spread across six sites: the jsonCache promise map plus five hand-rolled module-level promise memos with identical reset-on-error boilerplate; adding TTL/invalidation means reworking all of them
findings.suggestion: Wrap the memo pattern in one `memoize<T>(build: () => Promise<T>)` helper (with the reset logic inside) so the caching rule is a single policy point

findings.issue: One 700-line module mixes cache infra, URL policy, directory building and per-page DTO shaping; every data-related change funnels through it
findings.suggestion: Split into lib/api.ts (apiBase/fetchJson/cache), lib/directory.ts (species/generation/type caches) and per-domain query files

findings.issue: The generic card bakes in ability-specific 'Hidden ability' copy via a `hidden` prop, and pairs `showTypes` with an always-passed `types` prop — flag creep in the app's most-reused component
findings.suggestion: Drop `showTypes` (derive from presence of `types`) and move the hidden-ability note to a children/slot so the card stays feature-agnostic

findings.issue: spriteForId encodes the spec invariant 'species id == default Pokémon id' as an implicit assumption with no comment; if it ever breaks (the Deoxys scenario), the next reader must rediscover why it's safe
findings.suggestion: Name the invariant in a comment or constant (DEFAULT_POKEMON_ID_EQUALS_SPECIES_ID), or derive the sprite from the default variety when building the directory

findings.issue: A single monolithic stylesheet with per-feature class names; removing a feature (e.g. abilities' .hidden-note at line 226) leaves dead rules and requires archaeology
findings.suggestion: At minimum group rules by feature with comments; ideally move feature-specific rules into the owning components' files

findings.issue: No devDependencies and zero tests (0 test files); every edit above is verified only by the repo's external acceptance suite, making refactors riskier for future owners
findings.suggestion: Add a lightweight vitest suite around lib/format.ts and the query DTO builders — they are pure and trivially testable

summary: A well-seamed SolidStart v2 app on the current stable stack: fetching is confined to typed server queries, components are dumb and reusable, and the sprite-URL rule that scenario 2 targets is fixed in exactly one function. The drag on editability is copy-paste inside the single 700-line queries.ts — card-list construction, effect fallback, and cache memoization each exist 2–5 times — so cross-cutting fixes and new Moves-shaped sections are duplicated rather than shared. Net: comfortably average, easy to grep through, with three extract-a-helper refactors standing between it and excellent.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: The route itself is one deletable file and there is no nav link (app.tsx:23-26), but the query + interface (queries.ts:78-81,443-478), the Pokémon page's Abilities section (pokemon/[name].tsx:104-113), PokemonPageData.abilities (queries.ts:85,665,693), the card's `hidden` prop (PokemonCard.tsx:19,31-33) and .hidden-note CSS (app.css:226) all need touching; all findable via grep 'abilities', but dead prop/CSS would remain if you only deleted the directory.

scenarios.change: Fix the wrong-sprite-for-Deoxys-class-species bug in Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: Every card list (home, move 'Learned by', ability, type) gets its sprite through cardSpecies/spriteForId (queries.ts:184-196), so one fix covers all of them, and the detail page's artwork already comes from the fetched default-variety record (queries.ts:697-701), so it's unaffected. The only wrinkle: the fix relies on the implicit species-id==default-pokémon-id invariant, and if the real fix needed the variety's ID you'd extend buildSpeciesDirectory — still one file.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: The same `sort((a,b) => a.id - b.id)` one-liner exists in three server queries (queries.ts:371, 420, 463) plus the home page's client-side pageSpecies memo (index.tsx:100-104), so the 'sort' policy is edited four times. The `label` to sort by is already on CardSpecies, so each edit is trivial — but the duplication is exactly what a shared sortCards/cardsFromRefs helper would erase.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: The presentation layer reuses cleanly — PokemonCard, TypeBadge, displayValue, NotFound and the section/count-line markup are all generic. But the Moves 'shape' (fetch resource → 404→NotFound → build card list from learned_by → effect fallback) is not factored anywhere: getMovePageData (queries.ts:399-437) and getAbilityPageData (queries.ts:443-478) are near-copies, so an items query would be a third copy, plus new CSS in the monolith. Also note /items/:name would need a wildcard-aware route since item names contain no params issues, but the 404 route ([...404].tsx) requires no change.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: Excellent for the URL: apiBase() (queries.ts:132-138) is the single policy point, used by apiUrl/mediaUrl and spriteForId, with env fallback. Caching is weaker: the spec's promise cache lives in fetchJson (queries.ts:130,158-175) but five additional module-level memo caches (species 218, generations 258, types 315, home 340, version groups 497) each repeat the same reset-on-error boilerplate, so a TTL or invalidation rule means reworking six sites — mercifully all within one file.
